claims.text: The as-synthesized FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are initially solid.
The as-synthesized nanoparticles have an intended uniform bulk elemental distribution.
Cu atoms preferentially segregate to the nanoparticle surface during thermal exposure.
Cu has a lower melting point than the other constituent elements relevant to this proposed mechanism.
Preferential Cu segregation creates a Cu-enriched surface layer relative to the particle core.
A Cu-enriched surface layer has a reduced effective melting temperature.
The reduced-melting-temperature surface layer nucleates premelting.
After surface premelting begins, the phase transition advances inward as temperature increases.
Cu surface segregation is the primary factor governing the onset and progression of melting in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Nanoparticles with enhanced Cu surface segregation will begin surface premelting at lower temperatures than compositionally uniform nanoparticles.
Cu-enriched nanoparticles will show earlier surface diffusivity or structural disorder in imaging.
Well-homogenized nanoparticles will retain a solid-state structure to higher temperatures than Cu-segregated particles.
Controlled, sufficiently slow heating allows surface-diffusion effects to influence the transition.
Extremely rapid heating may bypass the proposed surface-segregation mechanism.
Catalytic supports or other external influences may cause alternative melting mechanisms to dominate.
Nanoparticle size, heating rate, and kinetic barriers may significantly affect the phase transition.
A mild anneal can be used to enhance Cu surface segregation, while a control treatment can maintain a uniform composition.
The hypothesis is falsified if Cu enrichment produces no statistically significant onset shift of more than 50 K or does not correlate with earlier transition.
